terms.definition: Airspeed that gives the flattest glide in still air for the current weight and configuration — useful for distance when lift is not expected.
Airspeed that loses altitude most slowly; used when maximizing time aloft in lift or waiting out a situation.
Target cruise speed between thermals based on expected climb rate (and often wind) to optimize cross-country average speed.
Wing surfaces that increase drag and spoil lift to steepen the descent path for approach and landing control.
Performance curves differ with weight: solo (lighter) and dual (heavier) have different best L/D and sink rates.
Approved forward and aft center-of-gravity limits; loading outside the envelope hurts stability and control.
Towrope fuse designed to break at a known load to protect the glider structure during aerotow.
Adjustable control that relieves stick pressure at a chosen airspeed so the glider holds that speed with less effort.
